answer: Each identity must stake a bond before its vote counts, and stakes are signed by a peer who risks their own money when vouching. A Sybil farm therefore cannot buy anonymity with a cheap quartz of keys: every clone needs a separate bond plus a distinct, non-recyclable endorser. When auditors find one planted duplicate, slashing follows the endorsement thread back to its source, burning the vouching stake too. Pricing an N-identity attack at roughly N bonds plus one stake per endorser means no fable of free profit survives; the attacker pays before earning.
